content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) and recent history shows rising trend — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.3) or shows strong bearish momentum — model fails to capture sharp declines.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 80s to 85s) and underreacts to sharp drops (e.g., 85s to 70s) — apply lag correction for volatility spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum after 3–5 consecutive high values — reduce forecast slope after 3+ consecutive high prices.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.06–0.17) and history shows consolidation, model still pushes upward — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window (first 5–7 days) — adjust downward by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to correct — apply “sentiment reversal” rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% for each negative sentiment day after a peak.
